faq.q: What types of QR codes can I create?
faq.a: Eight: plain text or URL, WiFi (SSID, password, encryption type WPA/WEP/none, hidden flag), vCard contact, email (with subject/body), SMS, phone number, UPI payment (UPI ID, payee, amount, note — builds a upi://pay link), and WhatsApp (wa.me link with optional pre-filled message). It builds the correct payload format for each type automatically.

faq.q: How can I style the QR code?
faq.a: Set foreground and background colours, choose square, rounded or circle dot shapes, pick a size from 128 to 1200px, and optionally use a two-colour gradient foreground. You can add a centre logo (PNG/JPEG), which automatically forces high error-correction (level H) to keep the code scannable. There's a warning to test with your phone before printing, since heavy styling can reduce scannability.

faq.q: Does it handle non-English text like Hindi or the rupee sign?
faq.a: Yes. It switches the QR library's byte encoder to UTF-8, so text containing Hindi, accented letters, the rupee sign or emoji encodes correctly rather than as garbage — important for UPI payment labels like "Pay ₹1,250". It generates entirely in your browser with no external QR API call.

faq.q: Can I make many QR codes at once, and export options?
faq.a: Yes. Batch mode takes up to 100 lines (one URL or text per line), applies your current style settings to each, and downloads them all as a ZIP with filenames derived from each line. For a single code you can download PNG or SVG, or copy the image to the clipboard as PNG. Your style preferences (size, colours, dot shape) are remembered locally; payload content is not stored.
